Evie: Quick follow-up from RFC-2025: proposal to add shape-aware quant profiles that adapt per-layer based on activation shape & observed sparsity. Thinking of an interface where the model manifest carries soft hints and the runtime decides exact bitwidth per kernel. High-level tradeoffs: ops-specific tuning vs runtime complexity. Thoughts?

Ravi: I like shape-aware hints, but we need a clear compile vs runtime boundary. Are these hints 'compile-time defaults' (used by kernel generator) or 'runtime suggestions' that can be overridden by the scheduler?

Evie: Good call. My mental model: manifest.hints are defaults used during compilation and for offline profiling. Runtime can override when telemetry shows degradation (e.g., drop to INT8 -> use FP8 for specific attention heads). So two layers: manifest default + runtime adjustment.

Kim: Curious about per-customer overrides. If a customer pins quality, do we let them opt out of runtime downlevels? Need policy: customer_override boolean in endpoint config? :thinking: 

Evie: Yes, something like endpoint.quality_tier = strict|balanced|aggressive. strict => runtime cannot lower below manifest minimum. Balanced => runtime can toggle within manifest range. aggressive => runtime can go down a lane for cost SLOs.

Max: Telemetry requirements: we need token-level quality signals or at least per-request loss proxies to decide overrides. Also hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping. Suggest metrics: perplexity_delta, degeneracy_rate, last_token_confidence.

Ravi: Implementation sketch: keep the manifest entry compact, e.g.:

```
quant_hints: [
  {layer_range: [0,3], hint: "int8", min: "int4", max: "fp8"},
  {layer_range: [4,11], hint: "fp8", min: "fp8", max: "fp8"}
]
```

Runtime reads hints, and we expose an ops-level API: allocate_kernel(layer, bitwidth_hint) -> kernel_id. The scheduler can call with adjusted hint.

Evie: That matches what I had. Two more things: (1) compat when new kernels not available -> graceful fallback; (2) versioning/compat of hint schema so older runtimes ignore unknown fields.

Kim: For product-level SLAs we should add a validation step when uploading a model: run a short shadowed pass across representative prompts to verify no >X% downstream regressions when runtime aggressively lowers. If it fails, warn or require stricter default.

Max: Ops playbook item: when a customer reports quality regression, we need to check last N requests for runtime-chosen bitwidths and whether fallback happened. Add runbook commands: `ri audit-quant --endpoint E --since 1h` that returns per-layer bitwidth timeline.

Ravi: Edge case: attention kernels where activation length changes (long vs short context). Hints should allow shape predicates, e.g. `if seq_len>2048 prefer fp8 on attn`. We can encode that as `predicates: [{type: "shape", seq_gt: 2048}]`.

Evie: Love it. Also add a confidence floor: if model returns low-confidence for >T tokens, force temporary increase in bitwidth for next M tokens. That deals with late-token degradation.

quant-bot: Auto-check results for RFC-2025 shape-hints: baseline shadow run (10 prompts) -> avg perplexity delta 0.6% for balanced, 2.8% for aggressive. See /reports/rfc-2025-quickcheck. :robot_face: 

Kim: Those numbers are promising. For aggressive we should surface which prompts degrade and attach to model upload review.

Max: One more operational constraint: image of kernel binary explosion. If we allow many bitwidth permutations per layer + shape predicates, build artifacts multiply. Need to cap to a small set and prefer fallback runtime adapters (shim conversions) rather than full kernel builds.

Ravi: Agreed. Implementation detail: canonicalize bitwidths to a supported set (fp8, int8, int4) and treat mixes via microkernels that accept packed inputs. Avoid N*M kernel matrix.

Evie: OK action items:
- Evie: draft a follow-up RFC section on manifest schema + example predicates (due Tue)
- Ravi: prototype runtime API for allocate_kernel + telemetry hooks (prototype by end of sprint)
- Kim: propose endpoint override UI + upload validation flow (spec by next Wed)
- Max: define audit CLI + required telemetry fields (PR by next Thu)

Ravi: Also doc the rollback semantics: when runtime increases bitwidth due to confidence floor, it should emit an event and optionally trigger shadow replay for audit.

Evie: Great. If no objections I'll start the draft. Thanks all :thumbsup: 

Kim: +1

Max: +1

Ravi: +1
